newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CSFB initiates Roche coverage with "buy".
newsitem.headline: CSFB initiates Roche coverage with "buy".

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB), investment banking arm of the Credit Suisse Group, said it had initiated coverage of Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche Holding AG with a buy recommendation, and saw a potential upside in the stock price of 25 percent over the next 18 to 24 months.

CSFB, which has taken over equity research from CS Research as part of the restructuring of the Credit Suisse group, said in a study the expected price rise is based on an expansion in Roche's Return on Invested Capital (ROIC).
Roche's ROIC is forecast to rise to 14 percent by year 2000 from 10.5 percent in 1995 based on the performance of its pharmaceuticals, vitamins and diagnostics divisions.
CSFB has a 12-month price target for Roche's non-voting equity securities, genussscheine, of 12,206 Swiss francs.
On Thursday Roche's securities gained 135 francs, 1.2 percent, to 10,985 francs after the company posted an 11 percent rise in 1996 sales to 15.96 billion francs.
CSFB forecast that Roche's Earnings Per Share (EPS) would rise to 457 francs in 1996 from 391 in 1995 and then to 532 in 1997 and 607 in 1998.
Roche's EPS is estimated to expand by 13.6 percent over the next five years.
Growth at Roche will particularly be driven by several new drugs, such as Xenical, Posicor, CellCept and Invirase, which by year 2000 should represent 22 percent of pharmaceutical sales.
In addition to this late-stage pipeline, Roche is strongly oriented toward biotechnology, which positions the company for growth well beyond year 2000.
CSFB also said Roche's management of its approximately 15 billion francs in cash and market securities have consistently outperformed many of the usual indicies over the past 10 years.
"Although we have no assigned any value to this asset management function, it is an incremental attraction to the stock," CSFB said.
